Huangshan (Yellow Mountain)

黄山 - Sea of Clouds and Ancient Pine Trees

Overview

Huangshan (Yellow Mountain) is famous for its "four wonders": bizarre pines, grotesque rocks, sea of clouds, and hot springs. Located in Anhui Province, this UNESCO World Heritage Site has been the subject of Chinese art and literature for over 1,000 years. The mountain's granite peaks, often shrouded in mist, create a mystical atmosphere that has inspired countless poets and painters throughout Chinese history.

Quick Facts

  • Location: Huangshan City, Anhui Province
  • Highest Peak: Lotus Peak (1,864 meters)
  • UNESCO Status: World Heritage Site since 1990
  • Best Time to Visit: September-November (autumn colors and clear skies)
  • Entrance Fee: ¥190 (peak season), ¥150 (off-season)
  • Opening Hours: 6:00 AM - 5:30 PM (varies by season)

🚗 How to Get There - Transportation

High-Speed Train

To Huangshan North Station: From Shanghai (2.5h, ¥150), Hangzhou (1.5h, ¥80), Beijing (5.5h, ¥350). Then bus to Tangkou (1h, ¥20).

By Bus

From Hangzhou: Direct bus to Tangkou (3.5h, ¥100). From Shanghai: Bus to Tunxi then transfer (5h total).

To Mountain Base (Tangkou)

From Huangshan City (Tunxi): Bus to Tangkou (1 hour, ¥20). Tangkou is the main gateway town at the mountain base.

Up the Mountain

Cable Car: Yungu Cable Car (¥80 up) or Yuping Cable Car (¥90 up). Or hike 2-3 hours from either entrance.

️ Recommended Tour Routes

Route 1: Classic Sunrise Tour (2 Days)

Day 1: Cable car up → Bright Summit → Stay overnight on mountain
Day 2: Sunrise at Bright Summit → Greeting Pine → Cable car down
Best for: First-time visitors, photographers

Route 2: Complete Huangshan (3 Days)

Day 1: Front mountain (Yuping area) → Greeting Pine → Lotus Peak
Day 2: Back mountain (Beihai area) → Monkey Watching Sea → Bright Summit
Day 3: West Sea Grand Canyon → Cable car down

Route 3: Express Day Trip

Route: Cable car up → Key viewpoints (3-4 spots) → Cable car down
Duration: 6-8 hours total
Best for: Short on time, good fitness level

Route 4: Photography Special

Best Spots: Bright Summit (sunrise), Lion Peak (sunset), West Sea Canyon (mist)
Tips: Stay overnight on mountain for sunrise/sunset; bring tripod

💡 Essential Travel Tips

  • Best Season: September-November for clear skies and autumn colors; Winter (Dec-Feb) for snow scenery but very cold
  • Avoid: Summer (July-August) is rainy season with frequent fog; National holidays (extremely crowded)
  • Stay Overnight: Highly recommended to stay on mountain for sunrise - basic but worth it
  • Physical Fitness: Hiking is strenuous; cable cars available but still lots of walking on mountain
  • What to Bring: Warm layers (cold on top even in summer), rain gear, comfortable hiking shoes, water, snacks
  • Book Early: Mountain hotels book out weeks in advance, especially for weekends
  • Weather: Check forecast - cloudy/rainy days reduce visibility significantly
  • Photography: Best light early morning and late afternoon; bring wide-angle lens
  • Altitude: Not extremely high (1,864m max) but can feel strenuous due to stairs
  • Payment: WeChat Pay and Alipay accepted; carry some cash for mountain vendors
